gen-dafont-nasalization-gf-noto-sans-nag: Round, stress-free curves with room between them. Nasalization looks like it was bent from one line, and Noto Sans Nag Mundari follows with a half-unwrapped c and s and lowercase rivaling its capitals.
gen-dafont-nasalization-gf-noto-sans-nan: Noto Sans Nandinagari keeps its openings generous at every weight, with short ascenders and a big lowercase body that never feels cramped. Nasalization adds round, heavy-walled letters.
gen-dafont-nasalization-gf-noto-sans-new: Nasalization looks like sign-shop vinyl, cut to a single line width with short ascenders and a floating, spaced-out stance. And Noto Sans Newa answers with a plainly open e and tall lowercase bowls, though shrinking the heading would blunt its charm.
gen-dafont-nasalization-gf-noto-sans-nus: Noto Sans Nushu reads tall, with a towering x-height and terminals held far from the stroke. Its biggest strength is the gap between Nasalization's dowel-round stems and that lofty plain sans.
gen-dafont-nasalization-gf-noto-sans-ogh: Tall bodies make Noto Sans Ogham look bold even though its e opens wide, while Nasalization brings stems like dowels and arcs like bent dowels. Big and short is where the heading shines.
gen-dafont-nasalization-gf-noto-sans-ol-: Bent-wire headlines meet solid word blocks. Nasalization runs its wire-bent look across each word, while Noto Sans Ol Chiki holds its curve tails back, so a long page would settle into dense, steady lines of sans.
gen-dafont-nasalization-gf-noto-sans-old: Noto Sans Old Hungarian opens large counters in its tall a, e and s, and those apertures stay open at tiny sizes. Nasalization does the stencil-cut work of one steady width, while Noto Sans Old Hungarian handles the plain sans reading.
Nasalization holds a constant pen pressure with short ascenders and spaced-out letters, set against Noto Sans Old Italic's tiny gap between x-height and cap height. It earns its keep big and short.
